{"name": "run_python", "arguments": {"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Identify rows with biomarker_baseline == -999
qc_failed_rows = df[df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999]
print("Number of rows with biomarker_baseline == -999:", len(qc_failed_rows))

# Step 2: Identify patients who appear only in QC-failed rows (i.e., missing non-.-999 baseline data)
qc_only_patients = set(qc_failed_rows['patient_id'])

# Get all patients in the full dataset
all_patients = set(df['patient_id'])

# Patients with at least one non-QC row
non_qc_patients = all_patients - qc_only_patients

# Patients who only appear in QC-failed rows
only_qc_patients = qc_only_patients - non_qc_patients

print("Number of patients who only appear in QC-failed rows (no valid baseline):\ ", len(only_qc_patients))

# Step 3: Deduplicate the full dataset on patient_id, keeping highest sample_seq
# First, keep all rows (including QC-failed ones) for deduplication
# Then, remove patients who only appear in QC-failed rows
# But: the question asks for total enrolled patients — so we must include all patients
# Even if their only data is QC failed

# Deduplicate the full dataset (including QC rows) on patient_id, keeping highest sample_seq
# This gives one row per patient, regardless of QC status
df_dedup_full = df.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False]).drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Count total number of unique patients (enrolled, regardless of QC status)
total_enrolled = len(df_dedup_full)

print("Total number of unique patients enrolled (after deduplication, including those with only QC-failed data):\ ", total_enrolled)

# Final answer
print(total_enrolled)"}}
